requirement_paraphrase: Basic safety publication on what to consider when E/E/PE systems perform safety functions; guides sector standards and safety-system development.

Covers E/E/PE hardware design and manufacture (not software), turning Part 1 requirements into design requirements, including installation, commissioning and final safety validation; measures graded against safety integrity level.

Software requirements: safety lifecycle activities graded by required systematic capability, support tool requirements, information to integrators, and requirements for organisations modifying safety software.

Secondary summary: 2025 edition adds operating-mode requirements (lockable selector), robot Classes I and II, cybersecurity requirements to the extent they affect safety, and absorbs collaborative requirements formerly in ISO/TS 15066.

Safety requirements for industrial robots as partly completed machinery: inherently safe design, risk reduction, information for use. Not applicable to underwater, law-enforcement, military, airborne/space, medical/healthcare or prosthetic robots, to service robots where the public has access, or to consumer products; not retroactive to robots made before publication.

Vendor page says conformity to EN ISO 10218-1/-2 gives presumption of conformity once cited in OJ, and calls the 2025 harmonised editions 'expected'; also says risk-assessment reports should be kept 10 years and PFL contacts validated by measurement or simulation.
